segments.text: Welcome to the daily Robotics news digest for November 5th, 2026.
Today we cover AGIBOT's AI breakthrough, LiberAI's new action model, and a major robot benchmark.
Tune in for the latest.
From Robotics & Automation News, AGIBOT unveils GO-3 Preview and takes top spot on three embodied AI benchmarks.
This report details the introduction of an embodied foundation model that has achieved first-place rankings across the RoboDojo, RoboTwin, and RoboColiseum benchmarks.
The GO-3 Preview model is an embodied foundation model designed to support learning across the entire lifecycle of pre-training, post-training, and post-deployment.
It utilizes an embodied-native WRAM architecture to unify task understanding, future-state prediction, and action generation.
Post-training is managed by Genie Evolver, which employs physical robots, simulation, and world models for continuous refinement.
The system incorporates Genie Master to allow robots to learn from operational experience and autonomously improve action policies.
This development indicates significant progress in integrating real-world experience into embodied artificial intelligence systems.
From The Robot Report, LiberAI Unveils Liber-0, a World Action Model That Grounds Human Experience in Robot Action.

This report details the introduction of Liber-0, a world action model pretrained on over two point two million hours of human experience, demonstrating the ability to enable zero-shot robot manipulation.

The system integrates human video, glove-recorded motion, and embodiment alignment to transfer human manipulation skills to robots by grounding human experience in measured motion and aligning it with the robot's body representation.
In a zero-shot evaluation across sixty GPT-6 tasks, the model achieved thirty-six point zero percent overall success without requiring task-specific robot demonstrations.
Incorporating glove recordings further reduces the necessity for specific robot demonstrations, which can lead to substantial savings in data collection efforts.
This advancement signals a significant step toward more intuitive and generalized robotic control systems.
From Humanoids Daily, RoboColosseum Launches Real-World Robot AI Benchmark With Unitree Support.

This report details the launch of an open initiative providing access to over one hundred robots and ten thousand free evaluation hours for testing robot artificial intelligence on physical hardware, revealing a significant gap between partial progress and completing full humanoid tasks, as initial tests showed only partial success on tasks such as carrying objects.

The initiative operates by using common protocols to standardize testing and releasing evaluation recordings for inspection, with Unitree supporting the project by highlighting its G1 platform for humanoid robotics, allowing researchers to apply for access to this infrastructure to test model performance in varied real-world settings.
This effort aims to standardize testing protocols for advanced humanoid robotics development.
From Robotics & Automation News, Pudu Robotics unveils a "One Brain, Multiple Embodiments"
strategy and showcases its full product portfolio in Europe for the first time.
This announcement details a strategy focused on establishing a shared technological foundation across diverse robot forms by combining reusable artificial intelligence with purpose-built hardware.
The showcased portfolio includes six product lines encompassing service delivery, commercial cleaning, and home lawn care.
Core technologies such as PuduFM and PuduAgent OS facilitate shared artificial intelligence capabilities across these distinct robotic platforms.
Pudu Robotics is concentrating efforts on extending robotics into varied real-world applications throughout the European region.
This development signals a potential shift toward standardized, adaptable AI solutions for physical automation deployment.
From MIT News - Robotics, "Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory"
details a new system designed to correct unreliable object descriptions stored in a robot's memory by incorporating uncertainty quantification.
This system achieves this by comparing multiple viewpoints and captions of the same object to assess the robot's confidence in its descriptions.
The method refines captions by selecting additional views that reduce uncertainty, leading to more accurate memory.
This process boosts confidence and improves the accuracy of object descriptions by up to five percent.
Ultimately, this method enhances a robot's ability to perform complex tasks by ensuring it remembers what it has observed with greater reliability.
This advancement enhances the reliability of robotic perception and memory systems.
Further research will explore the scalable application of uncertainty quantification in autonomous systems.
From Humanoid.guide, Agility Robotics closed a special purpose acquisition company merger ahead of a Nasdaq debut.
The story details the completion of the merger and the resulting listing of the company under the ticker AGLT.
Agility Robotics manufactures the Digit, a bipedal humanoid robot already implemented in warehouse environments for clients including Amazon and Toyota.
Development is underway for Digit 5, which will integrate safety features for proximity to people, with initial deliveries anticipated in the first half of 2027.
The company has tentative orders amounting to three hundred million dollars from prospective customers, while current revenue remains modest relative to expenditure.
Agility Robotics employs approximately five hundred personnel and is currently expanding its manufacturing and engineering capabilities.
This development signals continued progression in the application of humanoid robotics within industrial settings.
From Humanoids Daily, "NYU's MABEL Puts a 56-DOF Mobile Bimanual Robot on an $8,056 Open-Source Parts List".

This report details the release of MABEL, an open-source, mobile bimanual robot with fifty-six degrees of freedom, which was constructed using an open-source parts list costing eight thousand fifty-six dollars.
The design incorporates two seven-degree-of-freedom arms, two seventeen-degree-of-freedom hands, and a pitching torso.
This system is controllable through the Apple Vision Pro and an action policy trained on demonstrations.

The project is distributed under open licenses, including the computer-aided design, firmware, and simulation models, intending to advance humanoid robotics by integrating low-cost components into a complex, teleoperated platform.
This development signals a trend toward democratizing access to complex robotic systems through open-source methodologies.
From Humanoids Daily, KIST’s KAPEX Humanoid Reportedly Uses Over 90% Korean-Made Core Components.
This report details the development of a humanoid system where more than ninety percent of the core components originate from South Korea.
The project is a collaborative effort involving KIST, LG, and other partners aimed at the commercialization of this technology.
Various Korean entities are contributing to different segments of the project, including the platform design, artificial intelligence systems, battery technology, and manufacturing processes.
Core technology has been transferred from KIST to LG Electronics, with specific roles assigned across this partnership.
The objective of this endeavor is the development of a domestic humanoid industry through the demonstration of reliable system performance.
This development signals a significant step toward establishing a localized supply chain within the advanced robotics and artificial intelligence sectors.
From The Robot Report, "How GlobalLogic helped Haystack Robotics build a UV disinfection robot".
This report details the development of an autonomous mobile robot designed for hospital-grade UV disinfection with minimal human intervention.
The system achieved this through the integration of real-time perception and edge-based intelligence to safely navigate intricate hospital settings.
The platform was engineered as an expandable foundation, incorporating two operational modes: autonomous navigation and a follow me mode to facilitate caregiver assistance.

Development faced challenges related to establishing a justifiable return on investment, adhering to medical compliance standards, and successfully navigating complex human workflows within clinical environments.
This development signals progress in deploying advanced mobile robotics within regulated medical settings.
Future developments in edge AI applications are anticipated across various industrial sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Revo 1!".
This segment details the introduction of Revo 1, BrainCo's bionic hand for robotics, which achieves a Hand Score of five out of ten, placing it in the developing category.
The Revo 1 features a five-finger design and weighs 0.54 kilograms.
The construction utilizes an aluminum alloy and food-grade plastic.
The mechanism incorporates six precision micro motors.
The device is currently in production with a listed price of nine thousand five hundred United States dollars.
This development indicates ongoing progress in advanced prosthetic and robotic hand technology.
Further developments in this area warrant observation within the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, RY H6!".
This segment details the specifications and availability of the RY H6, a compact robotic hand designed for smaller humanoid platforms.
The device weighs 278 grams and measures 155 millimeters, featuring five fingers and utilizing brushless coreless motors with a force and position hybrid control system for operation.
The hand is rated with a dexterity score of two out of five and a strength score of one out of five, reflecting its focus on a small physical envelope.
The RY H6 is currently listed as in production with an advertised price of one thousand three hundred dollars, offering a commercially available option for teams developing smaller robotic systems.
This development indicates a trend toward miniaturized, specialized end-effectors within the robotics sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, RY-H5!".
This segment details the assessment of the Ruiyan Robotics RY H5 robotic hand, which received an overall score of four out of ten based on its evaluation.
The assessment included a Degrees of Freedom rating of two out of five and a Strength rating of two out of five, with both factors contributing equally to the total score.
The physical specifications of the hand indicate an all-metal body weighing zero point eight kilograms, and the product was manufactured in China.

The evaluation concluded that the item is currently a developing technology rather than a leading dexterous hand, and the RY H5 is listed in production with an advertised price of two thousand five hundred US dollars.
This information suggests ongoing development in the field of robotic dexterity and grasping mechanisms.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Dex3-1!".

This report details the introduction of the Dex3-1, a three-finger robotic hand designed for the G1 humanoid platform, with an initial Hand Score of three out of ten placing it in the developing category.
The device measures one hundred seventy-five by eighty-eight by seventy-seven millimeters and weighs zero point seven one kilograms.
It incorporates miniature brushless motors and is currently in production with an advertised price of one thousand six hundred United States dollars.
Research into the hand is recommended to focus on task performance assessing dexterity and strength in conjunction with integration requirements rather than visual appearance.
This development signals ongoing progress in the functional realization of advanced robotic appendages.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Are Drone Ports the Next Annoying Tech Neighbor?".
This report addresses residential concerns regarding noise and flight restrictions imposed by delivery drones.

Residential concerns arose when Amazon's delivery drones, specifically the large MK30 models, generated bothersome noise and flew lower than legally permitted, with acoustic research indicating the high-pitched whine of the rotors is particularly irritating.
Delivery drone companies are expanding rapidly, and while they promote positive uses, communities fear corporate overreach and safety issues.
Activists and local governments have responded by challenging regulations and advocating for community engagement regarding drone operations.
Ongoing disputes remain concerning noise, safety, and the legal regulation of airspace above private property.
This situation necessitates further dialogue between technology developers, regulatory bodies, and local communities concerning airspace management protocols.
And that's all the circuits we have for today!
AGIBOT's GO-3 is really booting up the AI world.
Thanks for plugging in and exploring the future of robotics with me.
Until tomorrow, keep building!
